metadata.note: The Houston East and West Texas Railway ('the Rabbit'), Houston - Logansport, La. (190.6 mi, chartered 1875, built 3 ft gauge in stages 1877-1886, standard gauge 1894), with its affiliated Louisiana leg Logansport - Shreveport (Shreveport and Houston Railway 1885-1890; Houston and Shreveport Railroad 1891-1927), and the Texas and New Orleans (Southern Pacific) through line that succeeded both on 1 Mar 1927 and ran passengers until 1954/55. The HE&WT had no branches (TSHA: Tyler, Waco and Sabine branches were projected, never built). HE&WT sections are separate features, each from its own opening year, so the map grows the line northeast in stages; all end 1927 at the T&NO lease (Rule 4 split, same pattern as houston_texas_central.geojson at 1925). The Louisiana leg is not drawn 1890-1891 (operator unknown between foreclosure and H&S operation). Freight afterlife (UP Lufkin Subdivision) not drawn (Rule 1). Research report: research/branches/houston_east_and_west_texas_railway.txt.
sources: Fowler, branchline.uk Louisiana railroads, route 69 (URL not recorded in the research report)

Official Guide of the Railways, Feb 1952 issue (schedules eff. 29 Apr 1951), Southern Pacific Tables 4 and 73 and station index (research/sources/official_guide_1952.txt, lines ~170265-170470, ~173779-173820)

not_yet_sourced: U1: HE&WT section opening years are construction dates (TSHA) and an ICC mileage-by-year table that disagree (Livingston 1879 vs 1880); the later year is drawn in each case. No first passenger train date is known for any section before the 26 Jan 1886 Sabine crossing. Houston - Humble/Cleveland service in 1877-1878 is possible but unconfirmed and not drawn.

U2: Passenger end 1954 vs 1955. History Center (Diboll): day trains ended Aug 1954, night trains Sept 1955; chicagorailfan: discontinued 1955; Clio (Nacogdoches depot): all passenger service through Nacogdoches ended Aug 1954. Drawn to 1955 (majority). A Railroad Commission of Texas order or a 'last train' newspaper story would settle it; the outcome of the 1954 Tex. Civ. App. case was not read (paywall).

U3: Whether the Shreveport and Houston Railway (1885-1890) and the Houston and Shreveport Railroad (1891-1927) ran passenger trains in their own names, or Logansport - Shreveport was served by HE&WT through trains over affiliated track. Drawn as their own companies and colours because the ICC calls the H&S the operating company; if they were HE&WT through trains, both Louisiana features should take the HE&WT colour. Also unknown: who operated Logansport - Shreveport 2 Jun 1890 - 23 Oct 1891 (left undrawn).
U4: HE&WT USRA operation dates (1 Jan 1918 - 29 Feb 1920) are assumed from the H&S ICC report; not split, per repo convention.
U5: The exact Houston entrance (the HE&WT's own pre-1927 Houston depot) and the Shreveport terminals (H&S depot to 1900, Union Station after) were not located; see each feature's geometry_quality.
U6: Gauge conversion: TSHA 29 Jul 1894; ICC only 'during 1894'.
U7: All headway_min and avg_speed_kmh values are estimates; no HE&WT/H&S-era timetable was read for frequency or running time.
Fowler shows 'Bonita Junction (stop for TNO only)' at MP 142 near Nacogdoches; not investigated, not an HE&WT line.

segments.note: Houston - Humble - New Caney - Cleveland - Shepherd - Goodrich. 3 ft gauge, steam from the start. Starts 1879: ICC valuation says 'By 1879, the line was operating to Goodrich'. TSHA has 20 miles 'completed' by April 1877 and Cleveland 'reached' in fall 1878, but those are construction words; no first passenger train before 1879 is documented, so 1877-78 is withheld (the start is the earliest CONFIRMED operating year, not a known first train). Ends 1927 because the HE&WT was leased to the Texas and New Orleans Railroad effective 1 Mar 1927 (TSHA; ICC valuation) — the operator change, continued in this file's T&NO feature. Not an end of service. SP held stock control from Oct 1899 but the HE&WT kept running trains in its own name, so no split there; USRA federal operation 1918-1920 is not split, per repo convention. Headway estimated, unsourced: the HE&WT is assumed to have run about one passenger train each way daily (or a day train plus a night train, the pattern the 1942 timetable shows); no HE&WT-era timetable was checked for frequency.
sources: Segment-level: start 1879 from the ICC valuation's statement that the line was operating to Goodrich by 1879 (TSHA's 1877/1878 construction dates bracket it); end 1927 from the 1 Mar 1927 T&NO lease (TSHA; ICC). Headway not sourced (estimate).

segments.note: Logansport - Shreveport. ICC: the Houston and Shreveport Railroad (inc. 9 Sep 1891) operated its own line 23 Oct 1891 - 31 Dec 1917 and 1 Mar 1920 - 28 Feb 1927 (USRA between, not split per repo convention). Standard gauge 1894 with the HE&WT. SP-controlled after 1899. Trains terminated at the Union (KCS) depot from 1900 (Fowler). Ends 1927 at the 1 Mar 1927 lease to the Texas and New Orleans Railroad (117 I.C.C. 504), continued in this file's T&NO feature. The ICC's 'operated the line itself' is a corporate-accounting statement; whether trains ran in this name or as HE&WT through trains is not established (not_yet_sourced). Headway estimated, unsourced.

segments.note: Houston (Grand Central) - Humble - Cleveland - Livingston - Lufkin - Nacogdoches - Timpson - Logansport - Shreveport. Texas and New Orleans Railroad (Southern Pacific), operating from the lease of the HE&WT and the Houston and Shreveport effective 1 Mar 1927; HE&WT merged into T&NO 30 Jun 1934 (no further split). Two daily pairs: day trains 25/26 (motor trains by 1942) and overnight 27/28 with Houston - Shreveport sleepers. 1951 service is POSITIVELY confirmed by the Feb 1952 Official Guide (Southern Pacific Table 4 'New Orleans and Houston and Shreveport' and Table 73 'Houston and Shreveport', 232 mi, sleeping cars, no motor-coach tag). Day trains 25/26 discontinued August 1954 (History Center, Diboll) after the T&NO's application to drop them was refused by the Railroad Commission and litigated (Tex. Civ. App., 24 Mar 1954). Headway 720 min reflects two trains each way daily — derived from the train count, not a sourced interval.

Headway derived from train count, an estimate.
